messages:
pager-bot: INCIDENT [P1] GPU decode node gpu-us-west-3-14 reporting repeated CUDA OOM during streaming decode. Error spikes -> ~14% request drops on /v1/chat/stream. Paging SRE oncall @alma (oncall).
alma (oncall): Acked. I'm on it, gathering logs and ticket context.
opsbot: alert/trace: spike start 2026-03-17T03:12:24Z; correlated rollout: ai-chat-v2 (r2026-0317-03). Related traces: https://telemetry.example/r/abc123
samir: Seen this pattern before when clients send huge max_tokens (header misconfig) or KV cache growth not bounded. Any recent traffic pattern changes?
alma (oncall): Collecting decode logs from node (last 120s). Pasting tail: ```RuntimeError: CUDA out of memory. Tried to allocate 2048 MiB (GPU 0; 24576 MiB total)
  at decode_loop.cpp:452
kv_cache_size=1.9GiB active_requests=42 streaming_sessions=39 max_tokens_header=16384```
devon: Node telemetry shows KV cache steadily climbing, GPU mem climbed to 98% before OOM, other nodes at 42-55%. This looks like a single-node flare (not cluster-wide). I'm cordoning gpu-us-west-3-14 from the router and starting drain now.
alma (oncall): Routing change: switching traffic off gpu-us-west-3-14 -> fallback pool (gpu-us-west-3-15, model: small-quant) to preserve latency for critical customers. Rolling update of routing policy in progress.
nora: Support note: ~120 failed requests in last 15m, 3 customers on chat endpoint got truncated/resets. Preparing CSAT-safe customer message.
kevin (sre): Quick mitigation suggestion: enforce per-request token ceiling at router for streaming endpoints and apply an override to lower max_tokens to 1024 while we triage. That should stop new spikes.
samir: I can hotpatch router policy. Endpoint: POST /api/internal/routes/patch body: {"streaming": {"enforce_max_tokens": 1024}}. Doing a coordinated hotpatch now (will push to region).
opsbot: deploybot: hotpatch job started by samir -> success (03:20:12Z).
alma (oncall): After routing + token-ceiling hotpatch I'm triggering a soft restart of the container on gpu-us-west-3-14 (docker restart + nvml reset). ETA ~90s.
devon: Restart done. Telemetry: GPU memory baseline returned to ~48%, no new OOMs in 3m window. Drain completed and node rejoined in warm mode.
alma (oncall): Reintroducing 25% traffic for canary to gpu-us-west-3-14. Monitoring traces and error rate.
nora: Customer update draft: "We experienced a transient increase in request errors due to GPU memory exhaustion on a single serving node. We applied mitigation and restored traffic; no data loss. We'll follow up with root cause and actions." Ready for send when we have final numbers.
kevin (sre): Root cause hypothesis: a client integration sent extremely large max_tokens (16k), bypassing earlier heuristics, growing KV cache until node OOMed. Actions: (1) router-level hard cap on max_tokens (reject >8k) + metric + alert, (2) additional per-request telemetry to log incoming max_tokens header for correlation, (3) throttle behavior for long-lived streaming sessions.
samir: Filed INC-2026-047 and attached logs + timeline. Assigning owners: eng-runtime/samir, infra/devon, sre/kevin. We need a postmortem and config hardening within 48h.
alma (oncall): :thumbsup: Closing pager for now. Status: mitigated. Will publish incident notes and CSAT updates once postmortem draft is ready.
